unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 16: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE AND FUTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project that envisions humanity’s future in space, exploring topics such as space exploration missions and predictions for life in the future. They will focus on creating detailed plans for hypothetical space colonies, interplanetary travel, and the challenges of living in outer space. Students will develop scripts for astronauts, scientists, and futuristic innovators who are involved in space explorations and technological advancements. Through role-playing, they will simulate missions, debates, and discoveries. They will use the target vocabulary and grammar to develop persuasive arguments, present scientific findings, and hypothesise about the future of humanity in the cosmos. The project will be presented in the class where they act out their roles, supported by visuals. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the universe and future with its components such as astronaut life on space stations; space explorations; life in the future'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what astronaut life on space stations; space explorations; life in the future mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the universe and future'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''planet, space, mission and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Astronauts will be living in lunar habitats in the future.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''astronaut life on space stations; space explorations; life in the future'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To express ideas about space explorations in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar through role-play activities. Activity 1: Mission to Space: A Role-Play Adventure Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigned them roles such as an astronaut, a robotics engineer, a biologist, or a mission commander. Each group selects a celestial body (e.g., Mars, Europa, or a newly discovered planet). The teams collaboratively design a space colony to solve environmental problems via space technologies. During the role-play, students present their plans to a ''Space Exploration Council'' (the rest of the class) using target grammar (e.g., ''By 2100, we will have established interplanetary communication''.) and vocabulary (e.g., ''lunar habitat, artificial intelligence''). They explain and support their ideas by answering questions and feedback, using question tags to make it interactive (e.g., ''Our space probe will have collected samples by 2050, won’t it?''). The teacher gives constructive feedback, and classmates select the most brilliant plan by voting via emoji cards. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To practise target vocabulary and pronunciation about space in English in context. Activity 1: Space Vocabulary Exploration The teacher begins by showing the visuals of space-related vocabulary, such as spacecraft, galaxy, alien, planet, comet, etc., with the English words written on them, and pronounces each word aloud. After this, the teacher distributes a worksheet to the students. The teacher says a word, and students find the visual that matches the word on their worksheet and raise it. For example, if the teacher says, ''This is a spacecraft'', students find the picture of a spacecraft on their worksheet and hold it up. This part helps students practice pronunciation and recognise new words. Then the teacher distributes the second worksheet to the students. This worksheet contains sentences with blanks. Next to each blank, there is a visual clue students have just worked on. Students look at the clue and write the correct word in the blank. For example, in the sentence ''By 2100, humans will colonise ________'', there might be a visual of Mars next to the blank, and students will write ''Mars''. After completing the sentences, the teacher gives constructive feedback on the students’ answers. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
